title: ThruLines #009
phrase: For well you know that it's a fool who plays it cool

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: Bowser was the greaser frontman of which doo-wop revival group?
questions.connectionNote: Na, na, na, na-na-na-na — the most famous coda in music runs four minutes on those syllables.

questions.subject: Life
questions.prompt: What's it called when a married couple officially calls it quits?
questions.connectionNote: Paul wrote it driving out to comfort five-year-old Julian Lennon during John and Cynthia's divorce.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.prompt: What do you yell when a golf ball might hit someone?
questions.connectionNote: 'For well you know…' — the first word of the line on the board is hiding in a golf shout.

questions.subject: Television
questions.prompt: What's the last name of Bryan Cranston's character in Breaking Bad?
questions.connectionNote: White — recorded in 1968, the same sessions and summer as The White Album.

questions.subject: Movies
questions.prompt: What was Wes Anderson's third feature film?
questions.connectionNote: The film opens on an instrumental 'Hey Jude' — Anderson built the whole introduction of the Tenenbaum children around it.

reveal.summary: Hey Jude. Sha Na Na is the na-na-na coda, the divorce is the one Paul drove out to soften for little Julian Lennon, 'fore' is the first word of the line on the board, White is the album summer it was born in, and The Royal Tenenbaums opens on the song itself. The line is the song's quiet center: don't play it cool.
reveal.ohMoment: The golf shout was the giveaway all along — 'Fore' is the first word of the line you were staring at.

editorial.notes: Q5 finalized per author: Wes Anderson's third feature (The Royal Tenenbaums, which opens on an instrumental Hey Jude). The author's alternate — a parrot sits 'on your shoulder,' echoing 'the movement you need is on your shoulder' — is a great fact for the reveal but awkward as a typed answer. Phrase trimmed at the rhyme break (40 letters).
